key_equations_and_data: §7.1 (line 451): tau_atm(lambda,d) = [tau_1m(lambda)]^d = exp(-gamma(lambda)*d); gamma = gamma_mol + gamma_aer. Units: gamma in m^-1, d in metres. Band form used by the pipeline (§13.4 line 1003): tau_B(d) = exp(-gamma_B*d).

§7.1 (line 458): L_path(lambda,d) = (1 - tau_atm(lambda,d)) * B(lambda, T_air). Band form (§13.4 line 1004, isaac-sim-spg skill line 136): L' = tau_B*L + (1 - tau_B)*L_B(T_air), with L_B(T_air) from the radiometry band LUT (or band_radiance_tophat).

§2 (lines 84–88): atmosphere multiplies the ENTIRE surface-leaving radiance (self-emission + reflected) by tau, then adds path radiance. The stage input is band radiance L (W m^-2 sr^-1), never temperature.
§7.3 (line 495): gamma_LWIR ≈ gamma_0 + beta*w, w in g m^-3 (absolute humidity — see inconsistency list re 'precipitable water'). Fit gamma_0, beta per band per atmosphere.

§7.3 (line 500): Magnus: e_s(T_C) = 6.112*exp(17.67*T_C/(T_C+243.5)) hPa (Bolton 1980 coefficients). Known answers: e_s(0°C)=6.112, e_s(20°C)=23.37, e_s(30°C)=42.46 hPa (published 23.39, 42.47 → 0.5% tolerance).

§7.3 (line 501): w = 216.7 * RH * e_s / T_K  [g m^-3], RH as a FRACTION 0–1, T_K in kelvin. 216.7 = 1e5 / R_v with R_v = 461.5 J kg^-1 K^-1 (water-vapour gas constant — add to irsim.radiometry.constants with source). Known answers: w(30°C, 0.80) = 24.3 g/m^3; w(20°C, 1.00) = 17.3 g/m^3; w(15°C, 0.40) = 5.1 g/m^3.

Koschmieder relation (NOT in spec but required to turn §7.2's 'visibility' index into gamma_aer): gamma_vis = 3.912 / V  (3.912 = -ln 0.02, the 2% contrast threshold). Per-band aerosol extinction = ratio_B * gamma_vis with ratio_B from the §7.2 table (fog: LWIR ≈ 0.13–0.27 of visible at V=200 m). Constant 3.912 goes in constants with source.
Derived starting coefficients from table midpoints (mark ESTIMATED): LWIR gamma_dry ≈ 0.36/km at w≈5 g/m^3, gamma_humid ≈ 1.21/km at w≈24.3 g/m^3 → beta ≈ 0.044 /km per g/m^3, gamma_0 ≈ 0.14/km.

§7.2 step 1 (line 469): 4–6 presets: US Standard 1976, mid-latitude summer, mid-latitude winter, tropical, fog/rain; plus haze. §7.2 step 3 (line 471): table indexed by (band, atmosphere, humidity, visibility) → preset YAML schema (new; §12.2 has no atmosphere section): name, provenance, valid_range_m (500), per-band {gamma0_per_m, beta_per_m_per_g_m3, aerosol_ratio_to_visible}, optional per-band sky dT_clear_k and q, optional per-band solar_zenith_transmittance.

WeatherSeries fields the atmosphere consumes (thermal-solver skill lines 97–98 + CLAUDE.md #6): air_temperature_k(t), relative_humidity(t) [fraction], cloud_fraction(t) (sky model), and visibility_m(t) — the last is NOT in the skill's field list and must be added (see inconsistencies).

Isothermal identity (the master Tier-1 test): if L = L_B(T_air) then L' = L_B(T_air) for every d and gamma. Radiance-space contrast identity: (L'(T1) - L'(T2)) / (L(T1) - L(T2)) = tau_B exactly. Segment composition: applying the stage over d1 then d2 (same T_air) equals applying over d1+d2 exactly.

Apparent-temperature anchor for tests (computed with band_radiance_tophat, 8–12 µm): L_B(310 K)=45.1149, L_B(290 K)=32.5169 W m^-2 sr^-1; tau=0.8, T_air=290 K → L'=42.5953 → T_app = 306.303 K. dL_B/dT(290 K, 8–12 µm) = 0.5672 W m^-2 sr^-1 K^-1, so 1 mK ≡ 5.7e-4 W m^-2 sr^-1.
gbuffer_ramp anchor: d=50 m, gamma=2e-3 m^-1 → contrast ratio exp(-0.1) = 0.9048374.
Thermal path radiance magnitude by band at 300 K (why SWIR path radiance is scattered sunlight, not thermal): L_B(0.9–1.7 µm) = 3.2e-7, L_B(3–5 µm) = 1.87, L_B(8–12 µm) = 38.5 W m^-2 sr^-1.

§5.3 (lines 305–314) sky/downwelling (ownership ambiguous, see decisions): L_down ≈ V_s*L_sky(theta_zen) + (1-V_s)*L_ground; T_sky = T_air - dT_clear*(1-cloud)*cos^q(theta_ZEN) [spec writes theta_el — bug]; dT_clear ≈ 55–70 K LWIR zenith clear-dry, 5–10 K overcast/humid; q ≈ 0.5–1.0; [R13]: LWIR sky ≈ -40°C at 15° elevation while MWIR reads > +10°C → dT_clear must be per band.

§5.4 (line 323): solar-path transmittance tau_atm^sun(lambda) for reflective bands — a slant path through the whole atmosphere, not the horizontal Beer-Lambert model; needs its own per-band per-preset parameter and air-mass law (deferred to build-order step 10).

§13.3 (line 973) / isaac-sim-spg skill line 122: path length d comes from the `DistanceToCamera` AOV, float32, metres — Euclidean distance (not z-depth). Sky/background pixels have no finite d and must bypass the stage (policy undefined in spec).

§1 fidelity ladder (lines 53–55): L1 = constant tau (d-independent override), L2 = band-averaged Beer-Lambert (TARGET), L3 = MODTRAN LUT. §7.4 (line 508) and Appendix A.2 (line 1387): dropped multiple scattering, adjacency, refraction, spectral fine structure within band; valid < ~500 m. Appendix A.6: no turbulence. Must be stated in README and an ADR.
float32 dtype contract (CLAUDE.md #2): distance, tau, L, L_air arrays float32 or float64; float16 rejected at the apply_atmosphere boundary.

work_items.title: Beer-Lambert transmittance and path radiance reference kernel
work_items.description: Create irsim/atmosphere/beer_lambert.py (pure NumPy, float32/float64 only): transmittance(distance_m, gamma_per_m) = exp(-gamma*d) (d may be +inf → 0); path_radiance(tau, L_air_band); apply_atmosphere(L_band, distance_m, gamma_per_m, L_air_band) = tau*L + (1-tau)*L_air. Guards: gamma >= 0, d >= 0, float16 raises, output dtype == input dtype. Provide a tau_override (constant-tau, d-independent) documented as the L1 fidelity fallback. Docstrings cite §7.1. This item has no dependency on weather, config or the thermal solver and can be built immediately after the Planck step, despite §16.4 placing atmosphere at step 8.
depends_on: radiometry: planck.py band_radiance_tophat (exists — used as L_B(T_air) oracle in tests)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Multiplicativity: tau(d1+d2) == tau(d1)*tau(d2) to 1e-12 relative; tau(0)=1; tau(inf)=0; tau(100 m, gamma=ln2/100) == 0.5 to 1e-12 (catches per-km vs per-m and sign errors).

Isothermal invariance: with L = L_B(T_air) (band_radiance_tophat 8–12 µm, T_air 290 K), output == L_B(T_air) to 1e-12 relative for d in {0, 10, 200, 5000, inf} and gamma in {0, 1e-3, 1e-1} m^-1 — equivalent to < 1e-6 mK (1 mK = 5.7e-4 W m^-2 sr^-1). Fails if (1-tau) is missing, if B is evaluated at the wrong T, or if the stage operates in Kelvin.
Contrast attenuation identity: (L'(310 K) - L'(290 K)) / (L(310) - L(290)) == tau to 1e-12 relative (linearity in radiance; a Kelvin-space 'contrast scaling' implementation fails this).
Segment composition: apply over d1=80 m then d2=120 m (same T_air) equals apply over 200 m to 1e-12 relative.
Convexity: min(L, L_air) <= L' <= max(L, L_air) for random L, L_air, d (seeded rng) — fails on a sign error in the path term.
gbuffer_ramp fixture at gamma=2e-3 m^-1: contrast ratio across the ramp == exp(-0.1) = 0.9048374 to 1e-6; output finite, dtype float32.
Dtype guard: float16 L or d raises; float32 in → float32 out; float64 in → float64 out (non-negotiable #2).

decisions_needing_adr.title: Band-averaged grey Beer-Lambert (single gamma_B per band) as the L2 atmosphere
decisions_needing_adr.why: Exact in d only for a grey band; wrong near band edges, for MWIR's opaque CO2 notch, and beyond ~500 m. The fit range (0–300 m) and the measured residual at 500 m (ATM-07) must be recorded so a reviewer can tell a deliberate approximation from an oversight (Appendix A.2, §7.4).
options: Scalar gamma_B per band per preset fitted over 0–300 m (spec §7.2 step 3; simplest; adding a band means adding a table entry to every preset)
Coarse spectral gamma(lambda) curve per preset, band-averaged against R(lambda) at LUT-generation time (bands stay pure data; handles unusual filters; needs a 1-D tau_B(d) table per band)
MODTRAN-derived tau_B(d) and L_path(d) LUT per preset (L3 of the fidelity ladder; needs MODTRAN access)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Provenance of gamma_0 / beta / aerosol coefficients
decisions_needing_adr.why: Without MODTRAN the only data is the §7.2 table, which lacks T/RH for the 'clear, dry' row and has an internally inconsistent haze row. The coefficients are therefore ESTIMATED; the ADR must state the assumed reference humidity (e.g. 15 °C/40% → 5.1 g/m^3), which midpoints were used, and what replaces them (MODTRAN runs, published LOWTRAN water-continuum fits).
options: Invert §7.2 table midpoints (now)
Run MODTRAN/LOWTRAN for the 5 presets and fit (when available)
Adopt published per-band continuum fits from the literature with citations

decisions_needing_adr.title: Aerosol/fog scaling across bands
decisions_needing_adr.why: The LWIR-in-fog advantage is 'the entire commercial argument' (§7.2) and its magnitude depends on droplet size: radiation fog (small droplets) gives LWIR/visible extinction ratios ≈ 0.1–0.3 as in the table; advection fog (10–20 µm droplets) gives ≈ 1. The chosen law fixes which fogs the simulator can and cannot represent.
options: Koschmieder gamma_vis = 3.912/V with a fixed per-band ratio from the §7.2 table
Koschmieder with an Angstrom lambda^-alpha law for haze plus a separate droplet-regime ratio table for fog
Mie-computed per-band extinction from a droplet size distribution (higher fidelity, more parameters)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Where visibility (and fog state) lives — WeatherSeries vs atmosphere preset
decisions_needing_adr.why: §7.2 indexes the table by visibility, but the thermal-solver skill's WeatherSeries field list omits it. If visibility lives only in the atmosphere preset, a scene can run dense fog in the atmosphere while the thermal solver sees clear-sky solar loading — exactly what non-negotiable #6 forbids.
options: Add visibility_m(t) (and optionally precipitation) to WeatherSeries; presets carry only fit coefficients (recommended)
Keep visibility in the preset and forbid mixing by a scene-level consistency check
Derive visibility from WeatherSeries RH/precipitation via an empirical fog model

decisions_needing_adr.title: Path radiance = (1 - tau_B) L_B(T_air) with uniform T_air, no elevation dependence, sky pixels bypass the stage, no scattered sunlight
decisions_needing_adr.why: §7.1 says path radiance varies with elevation; the model does not. In SWIR/NIR/visible the real daytime path radiance is scattered sunlight (thermal L_B(300 K, 0.9–1.7 µm) is 3e-7 W m^-2 sr^-1 — negligible), so hazy daytime SWIR will be too contrasty. The boundary between 'path to a surface' (this stage) and 'path to the sky' (§5.3 sky model) must be defined.
options: Uniform T_air along the path, sky pixels handed to the sky model (L2, recommended)
Add a veiling/scattered-sunlight term for reflective bands proportional to (1 - tau_aer) and solar irradiance
Elevation-dependent path radiance via per-angle sky temperature integration

decisions_needing_adr.title: Band identity key used by atmosphere (and material) per-band tables
decisions_needing_adr.why: §12.2 sensor schema has no band name; §12.3 materials and §7.2 atmosphere tables are keyed by band. Adding a band must not require code changes ('bands are data'). This is a cross-area schema decision owned by config but blocking ATM-03.
options: Add band.name/key ('lwir','mwir','swir','nir') to the sensor schema and key all tables by it
Key tables by wavelength range and match by overlap tolerance
Store spectral curves (gamma(lambda), epsilon(lambda)) and band-average with R(lambda) at LUT time — no key needed

decisions_needing_adr.title: Ownership and form of the sky radiance model (§5.3a)
decisions_needing_adr.why: CLAUDE.md scopes atmosphere/ to transmittance + path radiance; §5.3 places the sky model under scene radiance; no module in the layout owns it. It is atmospheric emission driven by the same WeatherSeries, and the spec's formula has an angular-variable bug and needs per-band dT_clear. Whoever owns it must also own the sky-pixel fill for ATM-06.
options: irsim/atmosphere/sky.py (same physics and weather inputs; recommended)
A new irsim/scene/ or irsim/environment/ module consumed by materials and atmosphere
Inside materials/ next to the reflected-environment term

decisions_needing_adr.title: Storage of atmosphere data: hand-authored YAML presets vs generated tables in data/lut
decisions_needing_adr.why: .gitignore excludes data/lut/*.npy and *.json while the ir-radiometry skill says LUTs are checked in with a hash. Atmosphere coefficients are tiny and must be reviewable diffs; if option 2 of the first ADR (spectral curves) is chosen, generated tau_B(d) tables need a home that is committed and hash-stamped.
options: YAML presets only (coefficients in configs/atmospheres, committed)
YAML presets plus generated per-band tables in data/lut with config hash (fix .gitignore)
Presets in YAML, generated tables rebuilt by make luts and never committed

decisions_needing_adr.title: Solar-path transmittance treatment for reflective bands (deferred)
decisions_needing_adr.why: §5.4 needs tau_atm^sun along a slant path through the whole atmosphere, which the horizontal Beer-Lambert model cannot provide. Deferring it is fine for LWIR but must be recorded so the SWIR step (§16.4 step 10) does not reuse the horizontal gamma by accident.
options: Per-preset per-band zenith transmittance with a 1/cos air-mass law (ATM-09)
Kasten–Young air mass with a simple Angstrom aerosol optical depth
MODTRAN solar irradiance tables per preset

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §7.2 table gives no temperature/RH for the 'Clear, dry' row, so gamma_0 and beta cannot be fitted from the two clear rows without assuming a dry-row absolute humidity (I used 15 °C/40% RH → 5.1 g/m^3, giving LWIR beta ≈ 0.044 /km per g/m^3).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: State the assumed reference weather in each preset YAML (reference_weather block) and in the ADR; cross-check the resulting LWIR clear value (≈0.36/km) against any published 8–12 µm horizontal-path curve (e.g. MODTRAN mid-latitude summer, 23 km visibility gives tau ≈ 0.93 at 200 m) before relying on it.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The 'Haze (5 km vis)' row's visible tau at 200 m (0.45–0.65) contradicts Koschmieder (3.912/V gives tau = 0.855 at 5 km); the row's values imply V ≈ 1.0–1.8 km. Either the label or the numbers are wrong.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Compute exp(-3.912*200/V) for V = 5 km in a test; pick one anchor (recommend keeping the visibility label and Koschmieder, re-deriving the row) and pin the choice with the ATM-04 test and the aerosol ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §7.3 RH unit is unstated (fraction vs percent) and w is mislabelled 'precipitable water' (a column amount in mm) while the formula yields absolute humidity in g/m^3 — a 100× or 1000× error waiting to happen at the weather-file boundary.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ATM-02 tests: w(30 °C, 0.80) = 24.3 g/m^3 ±1% and RH=80 raises; name the function absolute_humidity_g_m3 and have the WeatherSeries loader normalise percent → fraction with an assertion.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The single-gamma exponential in d is exact only for a grey band. MWIR (3–5 µm) contains the opaque 4.2–4.4 µm CO2 band (§12.1), so tau_B(d) is strongly non-exponential; a gamma_B fitted at 200 m will be wrong at 20 m and at 500 m in different directions.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ATM-07 quadrature experiment with an opaque notch: report the relative error of exp(-gamma_B d) at 20, 200, 500, 1000 m and put the numbers in the ADR; if MWIR error at 500 m exceeds a few %, adopt a per-band tau_B(d) table instead of a scalar gamma for MWIR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Isaac Sim 6.0 DistanceToCamera AOV semantics are unverified: units (metres vs stage units — USD assets are often authored in cm), Euclidean distance vs z-depth (DistanceToImagePlane), the value written for sky/background pixels (0, inf, or a large sentinel), and whether the annotator really delivers float32.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ATM-10 integration test: sphere at exactly 10.000 m must read 10.000 ± 0.005 m at centre and larger toward the frame edge (Euclidean); read one sky pixel and record its value; assert dtype float32. Do this before wiring the stage.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Sky pixels: if the atmosphere stage runs on pixels with d = inf, it outputs L_B(T_air) — but the LWIR sky is 30–60 K colder than T_air. The spec never defines which pixels get the Beer-Lambert path model and which get the §5.3 sky model.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ATM-06 sky-mask test (sky pixels bit-identical to input) plus a Tier-3 scalar check on a demo scene: sky region T_app on a clear night must be < T_air - 20 K in LWIR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The §7.2 fog rows imply LWIR/visible extinction ratios of 0.13–0.27, which holds for small-droplet radiation fog but not advection fog (ratio ≈ 1). The simulator may overstate LWIR's fog advantage — the headline claim of the product.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Add a droplet_regime tag to fog presets and compare the per-band ratios against published Mie extinction for 2 µm and 10 µm droplet modes; make the Tier-3 'fog kills visible before LWIR' test parametrised by regime rather than universal.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: In SWIR/NIR/visible the modelled path radiance (1 - tau) L_B(T_air) is thermally negligible (3e-7 W m^-2 sr^-1 at 300 K in 0.9–1.7 µm), but real daytime haze adds scattered sunlight (veiling radiance) that is not modelled. Hazy daytime SWIR/NIR images will be too contrasty.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: When SWIR is added (§16.4 step 10), compare the simulated hazy-day contrast against a simple veiling-luminance estimate ((1 - tau_aer) × sky radiance) and decide whether to add the term; record in the path-radiance ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: WeatherSeries does not exist yet and its specified field list omits visibility; the atmosphere's humidity/fog dependence (ATM-05) is blocked on the thermal area adding visibility_m(t) and settling RH as a fraction.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Agree the WeatherSeries interface (air_temperature_k, relative_humidity fraction, cloud_fraction, visibility_m, wind, solar) in the thermal area's plan before ATM-05; ATM-01–04 and ATM-07 can proceed without it.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: No canonical band identity key exists on the sensor config; the atmosphere (and material) per-band tables cannot be keyed reliably. Wavelength-range matching would mis-assign a narrow 8–9.5 µm LWIR filter.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Config-area decision (ADR); until then ATM-03 tests use explicit band keys and a test asserting every preset covers every band key declared in configs/sensors.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §7.1 says path radiance varies with elevation angle for a ground-based sensor, but the model has no elevation dependence. For slant paths to ground under 500 m this is second-order; for the sky it is handled only if the §5.3 sky model is implemented and used for sky pixels.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Tier-3 automated check: a horizontal ground path at 300 m and a 10° downward slant path of the same length give T_app within 0.1 K of each other (uniform T_air assumption is self-consistent); sky pixels covered by ATM-08 tests.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The fidelity ladder L1 'constant tau' mode (§1) is implied but not specified — whether it is a d-independent tau or gamma with a fixed d. Tests written for L2 will silently pass an L1 override that ignores distance if the override is not explicit.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Expose tau_override as a named parameter (ATM-01) and add a test that with the override set, output is independent of d and equals tau*L + (1-tau)*L_air.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The 216.7 factor in §7.3 is a rounded 1e5/R_v (= 216.68); the Magnus constants are empirical fits. CLAUDE.md says physical constants live in irsim.radiometry.constants — it is unclear whether empirical fit coefficients belong there or in the atmosphere module.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Put R_v (physical) in radiometry.constants with its CODATA/standard source and the Magnus/Koschmieder fit coefficients in irsim/atmosphere with Bolton 1980 / Koschmieder citations; note the 0.007% difference between 216.7 and 216.68 is irrelevant at the 1% test tolerance.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core: everything in ATM-01…ATM-09 is pure NumPy under src/irsim/atmosphere and src/irsim/config; tests/unit/test_layering.py already parametrises over every src/irsim/**/*.py and will cover new files with no change. Only ATM-10/ATM-11 live in src/irsim_isaac and import warp/omni.

#2 float32 or better: transmittance, path radiance, distance and band radiance arrays must be float32/float64; apply_atmosphere and apply_atmosphere_gbuffer assert dtype and raise on float16 (ATM-01 and ATM-06 dtype tests); ATM-10's integration test asserts the DistanceToCamera AOV is float32; the SPG kernel uses float32 textures/surfaces (ATM-11).

#3 Noise in radiance space: the atmosphere adds no noise, but it must operate on band radiance, never on temperature — the contrast-attenuation identity ΔL'/ΔL = tau (exact only in radiance) and the isothermal-invariance test (ATM-01, ATM-06) fail for any Kelvin-space shortcut, and the 306.303 K apparent-temperature anchor pins the radiance-space formulation.

#4 Kirchhoff closure: touched indirectly — path radiance (1 - tau) L_B(T_air) is Kirchhoff applied to the gas column (absorptivity = emissivity = 1 - tau); the isothermal-invariance test is exactly this closure (a blackbody at T_air is invisible through any path). The material-library closure test is not affected.

#6 One WeatherSeries feeds thermal and atmosphere: the Atmosphere constructor accepts only an injected WeatherSeries object, never a path (ATM-05 TypeError test, T_air(t) equality test, `solver.weather is atmosphere.weather` identity test); requires visibility_m to be a WeatherSeries field so fog cannot diverge from the thermal solver's weather.
#5 Aperture factor: not touched by this area (optics).
spec_internal_inconsistencies: docs/physics-model.md §7.3 line 495 calls w 'precipitable water (g·m⁻³)'. Precipitable water is a column quantity (mm or kg m^-2); the formula at line 501 (216.7·RH·e_s/T_K) computes absolute humidity / water-vapour density in g m^-3. Substituting a real precipitable-water value would be a ~1000× error.

§7.3 line 501 leaves the RH unit undefined (fraction vs percent). With percent the formula is 100× off. The thermal-solver skill (line 97) also says only 'relative humidity'. Must be fixed as a fraction and asserted at the weather loader.

§7.2 table line 479: 'Haze (5 km vis)' visible tau at 200 m = 0.45–0.65 is inconsistent with the Koschmieder definition of visibility (tau_vis(200 m) at V = 5 km = exp(-3.912·0.04) = 0.855); the stated tau implies V ≈ 1.0–1.8 km. The fog rows (lines 480–481) ARE consistent with Koschmieder (0.02 at V = d; ~0 at V = 50 m), so the haze row is the outlier.

§7.1 line 451 states tau = [tau_1m]^d spectrally; §7.2 step 3 (line 471) and §13.4 line 1003 apply a single band gamma_B. The identity is exact only for a grey band. §12.1 line 818 names CO2 4.2–4.4 µm as the MWIR limiter — precisely the non-grey case where a scalar gamma_B is wrong — and the spec never says over which distance range gamma_B is to be fitted.

§5.3 line 311: T_sky(theta_el) = T_air − ΔT_clear(1−cloud)cos^q(theta_el) gives ZERO depression at zenith (theta_el = 90°), contradicting line 314 ('ΔT_clear ≈ 55–70 K at zenith') and line 305 which parameterises L_sky by theta_zen. Intended form is cos^q(theta_zen) = sin^q(theta_el). Also, R13's ≈ −40 °C at 15° elevation implies a ≈ 55 K depression at only 15° elevation, which cos^0.5(75°) ≈ 0.51 × 60 K ≈ 31 K does not reproduce — the parameter ranges and the functional form are not mutually calibrated.

§7.2 line 471 indexes the table by (band, atmosphere, humidity, visibility) — visibility is an input — but .claude/skills/thermal-solver/SKILL.md lines 97–98 list WeatherSeries fields as air temperature, RH, wind, cloud, solar, optional precipitation: no visibility. CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 requires one weather object to feed both models, so visibility must live on WeatherSeries or #6 is violated by construction.

§7.2 line 471 keys the atmosphere table by band and §12.3 line 917 keys material tables by {nir, swir, mwir, lwir}, but the §12.2 sensor schema (lines 829–833) and configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml define a band only by wavelength range and response file — there is no band identity key anywhere.

CLAUDE.md layout (line 74) scopes src/irsim/atmosphere to 'Beer-Lambert transmittance, path radiance'; the sky radiance model of §5.3 (atmospheric emission, driven by T_air and cloud from the same weather) has no owning module in the layout (not materials, thermal, optics, or atmosphere). §7.1 line 461 even cites the elevation dependence of path radiance [R13] under the atmosphere section while the model there has none.

.claude/skills/ir-radiometry/SKILL.md line 66 says generated LUTs are 'checked into data/lut/ with a hash of the config'; /home/hunter/irsim-scaffold/.gitignore ignores data/lut/*.npy and data/lut/*.json. Any generated atmosphere table put there per the skill would not be committed.

§16.4 line 1305 places atmosphere at step 8 (after the thermal solver, step 6) with 'Tier 3 weather tests', and §1 line 54 lists band-averaged Beer-Lambert as part of the L2 target. But ATM-01/02/03/04/07 depend only on step 1 (Planck) and carry Tier-1 analytic tests; only the WeatherSeries coupling (ATM-05) and the crossover phenomenology need step 6. The build order over-serialises this area.

§5.4 line 323 uses tau_atm^sun(lambda) — a slant path through the whole atmosphere — under the same symbol family as §7.1's horizontal tau_atm(lambda, d). They are different quantities with different inputs (air mass vs ground range); the spec does not say which module provides the solar one.

§7.1 line 458 writes path radiance with the spectral Planck function B(lambda, T_air) while §13.4 line 1004 and the isaac-sim-spg skill line 136 write B(T_air) as a band scalar; the band-averaged product (1−tau_B)·L_B(T_air) ≠ ∫R(1−tau(lambda))B dlambda when tau(lambda) has structure — an additional, undocumented approximation inside the band-averaging decision.
